recipe_name: Best Ever Banana Cake With Cream Cheese Frosting
review_text: This cake was VERY good!  If you like banana bread, you will like this!  I took heed of the other reviewers and scooped out about a cup or so of batter and made a dozen mini muffins and put the rest in the 9X13 pan.  I found that my cake did not overflow this way otherwise it would have :-) This cake was done in my oven after an hour and 10 minutes at 275 degrees.  So depending on your oven, you might have to cook more or less.  Try checking after an hour and go from there. I let this cake cool for 20 minutes or so and then put it in the freezer for the 45 minutes.  Didn't like the idea of putting a steaming hot pan into the already packed freezer!  Anyways, the cake came out moist!  I altered the frosting b/c I myself am not crazy about super sweet cream cheese frosting but wanted a little cream cheese taste.  So I made a buttercream and cream cheese frosting by mixing 4 oz cream cheese, 2/3 cup shortening, 3/4 cups butter, 2 cups powdered sugar and one tsp vanilla.  This gave me a light, not too sweet frosting that I really liked on this cake.  It had the cream cheese taste, but was light, creamy and not too sweet. If making as directed, I would not put in all of the powdered sugar right away, as I think it might be too much. Check the taste after adding 2 cups and adjust to your taste! Kids and adults loved this. Thank you for the recipe Rhonda!

recipe_name: Fannie Farmer's Classic Baked Macaroni & Cheese
review_text: This is now our go-to recipe for mac-n-cheese. The first time I made it I used high quality white cheddar and American cheese slices (I was worried it would turn out tasting funky!) and the creaminess was out of this world. I added the American because the cheddar was really sharp and I wanted to subdue that a little. I had read somewhere that the white cheddar made for a less gritty cheese sauce and I feel that that is true. We made the macaroni again tonight but used just yellow cheddar and we actually skipped baking it because we got a late start on dinner. It still turned out really good. To make it without baking we simply mixed the cheese sauce into the cooked pasta and served (no bread crumbs, no baking). I do recommend baking, though, as the taste it amazing but if you're pressed for time it's also okay to skip that part. Also, we have a really large family so we needed to make more servings than this recipe serves. We did not double the roux part (flour and butter) but we did add more cheddar and of course more pasta. The sauce still turned out really thick; you can always thin it out with more milk if you find it too thick for your liking. Hope my comments help!

recipe_name: Kittencal's Buttery Cut-Out Sugar Cookies W/ Icing That Hardens
review_text: I used the frosting portion of this recipe for icing my Christmas sugar cookie cut-outs yesterday.  I was searching for a frosting that hardens and allows for easier, neater cookie storage.  Only after making many modifications, the frosting turned out.  Like other reviewers, I felt the instructions for the frosting were unclear in terms of the amount of milk.  Far more than 1 tbs. is needed to achieve the right consistency, so I would suggest indicating the exact amount (or an amount closer than just 1 tbs.) would be much more helpful.  Plus once I finally reached the right consistency, I realized the flavor was lacking.  I ended up whipping 2 tbs. butter, 1/2 tsp. lemon extract and 1/2 tsp. salt into the mixture for more flavor and less tacky texture.  The frosted cookies did harden, as the recipe title promises.  The trick must be the addition of corn syrup.  Next time, I think I'll just add corn syrup to my standard butter-based frosting recipe.  Thanks for sharing your recipe!  Although it didn't completely work out for me, I did learn a new trick in the process, so thank you for that!

review_text: It is 90 degrees outside and you might be wondering why I'm making chicken noodle soup on a day like today.  My neighbour is sick and really likes chicken noodle soup, so I told her husband I would make a batch for them.  I planned to use my own veggie stock, but adding spinach to it made it a nasty green colour that I don't think would be too appetizing for someone feeling unwell.  Luckily, I still had some normal veggie stock in the freezer, so I used that plus a 48 oz container of Swanson Chicken broth, low sodium/no MSG.  I followed the recipe to a T.  It was absolutely PERFECT!  I chopped carrots, green onions, celery, a bit of parsley and some  celery leaves and sauteed them for a couple minutes in just a bit of butter.  Added the broth, 2 cups of my good veggie stock and 1 tsp of bouillion granules. Simmered that on the stove til it started to boil and transferred to a 4 qt crockpot.  After that, I cooked three boneless skinless chix breasts in the remaining bits of the soup in the pot, cut those to small pieces and added to the crockpot.  There were a bit of bits on the pan from the chicken, so I added some water to that, mixed it a bit and added it to the crock as well.  I used egg noodles that I added the very last after running through cold water.   I'm kicking myself for not taking a photo of this work of chicken noodle soup art!  I did score a bowl b/c the crock was going to be too full and I gorged it down.  Thanks for a fabulous and EASY recipe, Miss Nezz.  This will be my go to quick and easy chicken noodle soup recipe!

I got a late start on it so I made it on the stovetop instead of the crockpot. I browned 3 pounds of cut-up boneless, skinless chicken breasts and lightly browned them in a little oil. I doubled the sauce recipe. Since I was indecisive on what kind of vinegar to use, I used equal parts of cider, rice and basalmic vinegar. I simmered the chicken in the sauce for 45 minutes and then added cornstarch thickener and some coarsely chopped colored bell peppers and broccoli florets. review_text: Sooo, I know this recipe was originally posted some years ago, but the results were so excellent that I had to join and post. After finding myself in possession of a rump roast (and not being handy with the whole beef thing) I came looking for directions. I dislike crock potted "pot roast" so was looking for a more traditional dry "roasted" experience. After reading the reviews, I followed the method 100%, using 2 cups of beef broth with a bit of Worcestershire, a metal pan and a 2.5 pound roast. 50 cooking minutes (uncovered) plus 20 resting minutes (under a foil tent), and I sliced into the juiciest, most perfectly cooked rare to medium-rare beef roast ever. Flavor was amazing and texture was succulent- lovely exterior crust from the searing and super tender interior. I sliced it very thin and ate it on a roll, French-dip style- perfection! I have a few more roasts in the freezer as they were on sale and cannot wait to make another in this same manner. I might have to start the Sunday roast tradition with this kind of success!

review_text: It took me a third try to get this cooked the way I like it. The first one that cooked for one minute was hard. The second one cooked for 45 seconds was too sloppy and under done for me. The third try worked like a charm. I have a 1,000 watt microwave and cooked the egg for 53 seconds. Next time I think I can cook it for 50 seconds and then just let rest in the water for a few seconds longer to continue cooking it gently. This is SOOOO much faster and much easier cleanup compared to cooking in a saucepan. Although I love poached eggs, I've never liked the mess of poaching eggs, so I started cooking soft boiled eggs... but even then I couldn't get the timing just right or they broke when I attempted to get the shell off. This is THE way to go for me from now on. Thanks PaulaG!

recipe_name: The Best Browned Beef Stew Ever
review_text: Really hearty and good! 4 men DD1 (5 years old), DD2 (15 months), and I say so. This recipe works well with all sorts of modifications, additional vegetables etc. I first put the stewing beef in a few tbs vinegar and Motts Tomato Juice for 35 minutes to help them become tender and give it some extra flavour. After I drained them and began the recipe. I used white rice flour instead of regular flour to be gluten free. Before I added the big pieces of vegetables I cooked the meat for approximately 40 minutes longer than called for in recipe#206712 instead of beef broth as I could make it easier. I used 3 medium carrots in all, cut into big chunks rather than diced or chopped fine for more heartiness. I used one less onion than called for, though my onions were pretty big. I exchanged the thyme to marjoram due to personal preference. In addition to the called for vegetables I added some chunks of butter nut squash one time (wouldnt do it again), a large handful of fried okra one time which was a good addition, and about 1/3 cup frozen baby peas near the end of cooking time both times. I served it with quinoa macaroni if wished. I would make again during the winter for a warming lunch or dinner.

1)For the shortening I substituted 1/3 cup canola oil and 1/2 natural (no sugar added) apple sauce, which, conveniently is the exact amount in one of the snack packs
2)I reduced the sugar to 2/3 cup, equal parts white and brown. This definitely resulted in a less sweet cookie, so I might consider 1 cup next time.
3)I used 2 cups old-fashioned oats instead of quick oats.
4) I used 9 oz (3/4 of the bag) of chocolate chips.
I used a tablespoon measure to scoop out the dough, resulting in larger cookies.  The recipe made 3 dozen cookies this way.  I baked them for 12 minutes at 350. Very chewy and moist cookie. Probably not as yummy as the original, but a keeper for my kids's lunchbox snacks and for keeping around the house!
